_comment: Account boundary of the game front: what authorises /login to rotate an account's session (and so retire the pcuid a client is playing on) and what authorises /create_player to write a profile name. The HTTP front carries no credential at login - Login.cs:20 posts web_id/area_id/user_id=<Account.DataID>/bypass_auth=true/guest and Login.cs:31 returns the session_id that every later request posts back as pcuid - so a refid on its own used to be the identity: /login evicted the real player (durable on the profile document, handlers/utils.ts tombstoneSessionOnProfile) and create_player renamed any account (CreatePlayer.cs:19 posts name+user_id with no session). The credential this server can actually check is the e-Amusement card presentation, because the card flow is the same process: cardmng.inquire (CardEntryScene.cs:462) and cardmng.getrefid (CardEntryManager's new-card path) are the only requests carrying a 16-hex card id, and handlers/eamuse.ts stamps each canonical one onto the account's own document (profile.card_auth, handlers/utils.ts recordCardAuthIntent). The refid a login carries is then a claim, honoured for an account bound to a credential (profile.card_id, from saveCardToProfile) only when that credential was presented inside card_auth_window_seconds AND not already spent: one card scan authorises exactly one login (ExecLoadAtCardEntry calls Login once, GameDataManager.cs:139), because a stamp left open for the window is a bearer token for the next caller who knows the refid. handlers/utils.ts consumeCardCredential spends it; the next cardmng call re-mints it. Card-bound accounts are the hard boundary: a bearer claim without a spendable card credential is refused whatever the idle clock says, and create_player cannot rename one. TRUST MODEL for card-less accounts, recorded because the deployment has to be able to say it: an account with no bound credential has nothing the server can check, so CROSS-ACCOUNT ISOLATION IS OUT OF THE TRUST MODEL FOR IT - that is the honest description of card-less play (the -AUTOSERVE lanes' fixed guest dataid MFGTESTGUEST1 per AccountGameData.cs:70-74, the WebGL browser lane, any cardless deployment). The server cannot tell such a holder re-logging in from a stranger: the shipping client itself logs in a second time while its own session is still working - measured 2026-11-01 on the WebGL lane, whose boot re-login lands at session_idle=0s - and refusing that refusal breaks the client's own boot path, so card-less login rotates the session: last login wins, the evicted pcuid is tombstoned to 770 (the client's own re-login path), exactly as the original front behaved. takeover_grace_seconds therefore defaults to 0. A positive number re-arms the idle rule as an opt-in throttle: until the account's live session has been idle that long (or the holder /logs out - Logout.cs:16 posts pcuid, sent by GameoverFlow.cs:88 at Gameover), a card-less takeover is refused; a deployment that sets it accepts that its own clients re-logging in inside the window are locked out until the session cools. mode: 'card' (default) enforces this, 'off'|'none'|'open' turns the whole gate off - a deployment that wants the fully open behaviour has to say so here or in VFG_ACCOUNT_AUTH. Override per deployment with VFG_ACCOUNT_AUTH=card|off, VFG_CARD_AUTH_WINDOW=<seconds>, VFG_SESSION_TAKEOVER_GRACE=<seconds, 0 disables the idle rule>.
